endorsements.quote: Accordingly, we target evidence along four axes: i) multisite external validation to quantify out-of-distribution generalization; ii) counterfactual validity tested on heldout perturbations with standardized effect-size metrics; iii) probabilistic calibration (e.g., reliability analyses) and decision-analytic value (e.g., net benefit); and iv) subgroup fairness audits across sex, ancestry, and disease stage.

Reporting is harmonized to contemporary guidance—TRI- POD+AI for prediction studies [ 52], ‘Developmental and Exploratory Clinical Investigations of Decision-support systems driven by Artificial Intelligence (DECIDE-AI)’ for early/live evaluations of decision support [ 58], and ‘Stan dard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials-Artificial Intelligence (SPIRIT-AI)’/CONSORT-AI for AI trial protocols and reports—so development, validation, and trialing are transparent and reproducible [59].

Accordingly, we target evidence along four axes: i) multisite external validation to quantify out-of-distribution generalization; ii) counterfactual validity tested on heldout perturbations with standardized effect-size metrics; iii) probabilistic calibration (e.g., reliability analyses) and decision-analytic value (e.g., net benefit); and iv) subgroup fairness audits across sex, ancestry, and disease stage.
Model stewardship should move beyond static performance reports to monitored deploy ment with prespecified drift thresholds and action plans, including human-in-the-loop overrides.

Credibility should scale with intended use and decision risk, echoing the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)’s risk-informed framework—built on the American Society of Mechanical Engineers Verification and Valida tion 40 (ASME V&V 40)—for assessing computational models [57].

unlisted_practices: Quantify the utility-privacy trade-offs of privacy-preserving learning rather than assuming them.
Harmonize ontologies and data models for cell types, assays, and outcomes to enable cross-study learning.
Use federated learning to train and update models across institutions without sharing raw data.
Establish regulatory sandboxes for the clinical use of AI under health-sector regulators.
Develop credibility frameworks for in silico evidence, such as virtual clinical trials, aligned with decision risk.
Build global multicenter data-sharing and validation networks that embed external validation and equity metrics.
Ensure participation and benefit for low- and middle-income countries in AI development and deployment.

screen.reason: This is a framework and perspective article outlining a methodological roadmap, governance, and verification concepts for AI virtual cells in nephrology, rather than an empirical study.
